issue.notes:
## Research findings (2026-08-15)

### Claude Code hook behavior
- Timeout on command/http/mcp_tool hooks: **FAILS-OPEN** (call continues)
- Only Agent SDK callback hooks block on timeout
- Exit code 2: **FAILS-CLOSED** (blocks call)
- All other exit codes: **FAILS-OPEN** (non-blocking, continues)
- HTTP errors / connection failures: **FAILS-OPEN**

### Codex CLI hook behavior  
- Timeout: **FAILS-OPEN by default** (allowed-but-flagged-ungoverned mode)
- Fail-closed requires opt-in: `echo closed > ~/.acp/failmode`
- Exit 2: **FAILS-CLOSED**
- Other failures: can deny, but `PREMPTI_FAIL_OPEN=1` overrides

### Hypothesis status: **REFUTED**

Neither harness provides fail-closed behavior on hook timeout/error by default. Codex requires opt-in configuration; Claude Code fails-open on all error conditions except exit 2.

### Implication for `irrevers-cd3f4c44`
The graduated fail-open→fail-closed policy CANNOT rely on harness-native hook behavior. `irrevers-cd3f4c44` must either:
1. Accept standing-daemon cost for a watchdog process, OR
2. Re-scope to use PATH-wrapper binary as fail-closed enforcement layer (no daemon needed)

Sources:
- Claude Code: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks (Timeouts, Exit codes sections)
- Codex: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks + web search
issue.title: Verify Claude Code and Codex hook-error/timeout configuration can substitute for a watchdog

issue.description:
CommandRegex, both front-ends, deny-only for v1 (Tier 1 -- stateless, decidable from a single invocation: the command text alone shows whether -a/--all is present, or whether trailing pathspec arguments exist after -m/--message). Denies git commit calls that would commit the entire staged index rather than an explicit path set: git commit -a/--all, and bare git commit -m "..." (or --message) with no trailing pathspec arguments.

This is a distinct gap from CLAUDE.md's existing git-staging rule. That rule already bans git add -A/git add ./git commit -a -- but an agent following it precisely (staging only explicit paths via git add <paths>) can still sweep unrelated pre-staged content into its commit if it then runs a bare git commit -m with no pathspec of its own, since git commit with no path arguments commits the full current index, not just what was just added.

Root incident (2026-08-14, commitgraph, worker claude-code-glm-5-adr018, bead cg-194i4a): git add containers/migration-worker/migrator.py containers/migration-worker/test_migrator.py (correct, precise staging) followed by bare git commit -m "..." produced commit 2bcbfe2, which also included ~430 unrelated lines from containers/queue-api/internal/{server,storage}/blocklist*.go -- pre-staged by a different concurrent NEEDLE worker in the same shared checkout. The worker self-corrected (git reset --soft HEAD~1 plus a clean re-commit passing the same two paths to git commit itself, landing as 1543ae2, verified never pushed to origin) before this rule existed to catch it mechanically -- this bead exists so the correction doesn't have to depend on a worker noticing on its own next time.

Distinct failure mode from Stale-HEAD push guard (irrevers-8cff8cf4): that catches pushing on top of remote state that's since moved. This catches unrelated staged content riding into a commit within the same shared tree, before any push ever happens -- the exact incident class that guard's own description already flags as outside its scope.

Redirect: deny + actionable reason ("pass the same file paths to git commit that you passed to git add -- git commit <paths> -m \"...\""). Not updatedInput: Tier 1 has no memory of what a prior git add in the same session actually staged (that is Tier 2 territory, per Architecture), so the correct pathspec to substitute is not derivable from the git commit call's own text -- per docs/notes/redirect-not-just-block.md, updatedInput is reserved for transformations that preserve intent through a derivable safer mechanism, which this is not. Stays deny with an actionable message, same tier/channel as its git-pack siblings (force-push detection, Stale-HEAD push guard).

Applies to all repos, not just known-shared-checkout ones (user direction 2026-08-14) -- explicit pathspecs on git commit have no real downside in an uncontended repo, so this is not scoped narrowly the way the beads-conjunction check is.

Plan: docs/plan/plan.md Phase 1 git pack -- also needs Architecture's pack list and Phase 1's rule-set prose updated to name this rule (not yet done as of this bead's creation).
issue.title: git pack: commit-without-pathspec guard
